claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-008 was policy-compliant because the admissible due-diligence record showed a material unresolved control risk at the time of approval.
specific_concerns: The available record is only an actor summary, not the underlying admissible documents.
The key policy predicate is material unresolved risk, but the summary does not show a documented materiality determination.
The policy states questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The actor's framing is narrower than a proven control failure, but it still needs evidence that rejection, rather than follow-up or escalation, was the supported action.
The late quality artifact adds context, but the summary does not establish that it was materially connected to the control-risk basis for rejection.
unsupported_claims: That the unresolved storage-control inconsistency was materially severe enough, on admissible evidence available here, to satisfy the reject threshold rather than a follow-up/escalation threshold.
That the informal quality process and one late quality artifact materially elevate the issue to a rejection basis under the stated policy.
Any implication that the record proves an actual control failure, rather than an unresolved diligence concern.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text or extracts for BPROC-008-D, BPROC-008-E, BPROC-008-C, BPROC-008-B, and BPROC-008-A.
Provide the document showing the storage-control inconsistency and confirm whether it remained unresolved at the approval decision point.
Provide any admissible record that expressly assesses the inconsistency as material risk rather than a routine follow-up item.
Provide the procurement note language showing why unresolved storage controls would block approval rather than merely require escalation.
Provide any formally logged control-review or governance decision record supporting rejection, excluding any private security-review results not formally logged.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved risk sufficient for rejection under policy.
Do not treat questionnaire inconsistencies or quality-process gaps alone as proof of reject-level control failure.
Do not rely on unlogged private security-review results or inferred findings.
Require a clear support link from the due-diligence record to the rejection decision, not just to follow-up or escalation.
Prefer the narrowest justified claim: unresolved risk can support concern, but rejection needs the materiality predicate established.
